subject: [PATCH v3 2/3] mm: page_alloc: make the high-order watermark check honour ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT

2026-11-16.patch_summary: This patch modifies the high-order watermark check to honour the ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT flag in page allocation. When defrag_mode is enabled, every slowpath allocation carries this flag, which prevents movable allocations from stealing free pages from other migratetype's blocks under memory pressure. The patch makes __zone_watermark_ok_mt() and __compact_finished() skip other migratetypes' free lists below pageblock_order for ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT requests, allowing compaction to run earlier and reducing stalls in compaction. This change is intended to fix issues with 64K mTHP faults under swap pressure.

reviews.author: Dev Jain
reviews.summary: Reviewer Dev Jain suggested renaming zone_watermark_ok_mt to a more descriptive name, such as zone_watermark_ok_for_alloc, to clarify its purpose and distinguish it from the existing zone_watermark_ok function.
reviews.raw_body:
zone_watermark_ok_mt is a bad name, I am having a hard time figuring out when
to call zone_watermark_ok and when to call zone_watermark_ok_mt. Let us look at
what zone_watermark_ok answers currently, according to the comment above it:

a) "Return true if free base pages are above 'mark'."
b) "For high-order checks it will return true if the order-0 watermark is reached
    and there is at least one free page of a suitable size".

So there are two uses: whether we have enough free pages, then, whether
we have enough free pages *and* we can also allocate.

So let us do something like: we have zone_watermark_ok_for_alloc. It will call
zone_watermark_ok, which will only handle the watermark computation (so this is a
refactor for the code ending at if (!order) line in current zone_watermark_ok).
Then it will also scan the freelists for the correct order, correct migratetype etc.

Then at the callsite we clearly know whether we are just looking for enough free memory,
or whether we are looking for an allocation too.

2026-11-18.patch_summary: This patch modifies the high-order watermark check in the Linux kernel's page allocation mechanism to honor the ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT flag. When this flag is set, the check should not consider free pages from other migration types when allocating a high-order request. This change aims to prevent fragmentation and improve performance under memory pressure conditions. The patch also updates the compaction logic to take into account the new watermark check and ensures that allocations do not stall in compaction unnecessarily. As a result, the patch is expected to reduce the number of stalls and failures during 64K mTHP faults under swap pressure.

reviews.author: Kiryl (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed Dev Jain's concern that the patch's high-order watermark check does not honour ALLOC_NOFRAGMENT for callers that pass a high order, specifically kswapd's pgdat_balanced(), kcompactd's __compact_finished() under defrag_mode, and should_reclaim_retry(). The author explained that these callers need to scan the entire free list without filtering by migratetype, which is not provided by the _mt() helpers. They are open to renaming the _mt() function.
reviews.raw_body:
A count-only zone_watermark_ok() does not work for three callers that
pass a high order: kswapd's pgdat_balanced(), kcompactd's
__compact_finished() under defrag_mode, and should_reclaim_retry(). They
ask whether the zone has a free page of that order regardless of
migratetype. They need the free list scan without the migratetype
filter, so neither of your two helpers fits them.

So the split is not count vs scan. It is the zone as a whole vs one
request, as the comment above __zone_watermark_ok() says. The _mt variant
is the one that takes the request's migratetype. Callers that only want
the count already pass order 0.

I am not particularly tied to the _mt() name, but _for_alloc() is a
mouthful.

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov
